classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: Final manufacture in UAE PASS; minimal operations PASS; CTSH PASS (all non-originating inputs classified outside subheading 761010); VA PASS (build-down 49.0% against threshold 45%, FOB basis).

procedure.step: Ensure the factory is registered through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service, which requires the factory to be outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Prepare the application for a Certificate of Origin for India, including the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product; each item must qualify separately in its own right.
Log in to the ministry e-services portal and choose the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Fill in the application form, upload proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, if a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online: AED 50 (invoice value up to AED 100000).
Submit the application and receive approval, or a return with comments to correct.
Print the approved certificate; it must be issued prior to, at, or within five working days of export.
The certificate is valid for twelve months from issue, covers only one import, and may list several products.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of issue.
If the invoice is issued by a third party, indicate 'third-party invoicing' on the certificate.
Goods must be shipped directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading or storage.
A lost certificate can be replaced by a certified true copy.
An issued certificate can be amended once for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and destination cannot be changed.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
India's certificate form uses box 9 for remarks, while the agreement says box 8; India's form governs entry into India.
The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 via LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
The certificate fee assumes the invoice value equals the shipment value given.
